Jerome H. Powell: Given the current economic conditions of low inflation and very high unemployment, the Committee should not raise the federal funds rate at its next meeting. Maintaining the current low rate supports economic recovery and aligns with our commitment to achieving maximum employment and price stability.

Given the current high unemployment and low inflation well below our 2% target, it is not appropriate to tighten policy now. The Committee should wait for more data before considering any policy tightening.
Given the current economic conditions, it is not urgent to increase the level of policy restriction. Our focus remains on supporting the economy and ensuring ample reserves to maintain stability.

Given the current economic conditions with very low inflation and exceptionally high unemployment, I would not support a 25 basis point hike at the coming meeting. Our priority should be to support the economic recovery by maintaining accommodative monetary policy.

Given the severe economic downturn and elevated unemployment, the time has not yet come to firm the policy stance; instead, we should maintain or move toward a more accommodative monetary policy to support recovery. Premature tightening could hinder the fragile economic rebound.
John C. Williams: Given the exceptionally high unemployment rate and inflation well below the 2% target, the Committee should maintain the current federal funds rate and not raise it at the next meeting. It is essential to keep monetary policy highly accommodative to support the economic recovery.

Given the substantial labor market slack and inflation well below target, it is not appropriate to tighten policy now. The Committee should wait for more data before considering any policy tightening.

Given the current economic conditions of low inflation and very high unemployment, it is not urgent to increase policy restriction. Maintaining the current accommodative stance is appropriate to support the ongoing recovery.

Given the severe economic downturn and elevated unemployment, I do not support a 25 basis point hike at the coming meeting; monetary policy should remain accommodative to support recovery. Maintaining the current federal funds target range is appropriate until we see substantial improvement in labor market conditions and inflation moving sustainably toward our 2% goal.

The time has not yet come to firm the policy stance further given the persistently high unemployment and inflation well below target. We must maintain our highly accommodative monetary policy and forward guidance to support the ongoing economic recovery.
Michelle W. Bowman: The Committee should not raise the federal funds rate at its next meeting given the very low inflation and extremely high unemployment. Maintaining the current accommodative stance is essential to support the economic recovery.

Given the current low inflation and very high unemployment, it is not appropriate to tighten policy now; the Committee should wait for more data to assess the economic recovery before considering any rate increases. Maintaining accommodative policy supports the labor market and helps move inflation back toward our 2% target.

Given the current low inflation and extremely high unemployment, it is not urgent to increase policy restrictions; instead, accommodative policy should remain in place to support economic recovery. Premature tightening risks undermining progress toward full employment and inflation normalization.

Given the current low inflation well below target and the exceptionally high unemployment rate, I would not support a 25 basis point hike at the coming meeting. Our focus should remain on supporting the economy and achieving maximum employment before considering tightening monetary policy.

Given the severe economic downturn and elevated unemployment, the Federal Reserve should maintain its highly accommodative policy stance rather than firming it further at this time. Premature tightening risks undermining the fragile recovery and delaying progress toward our inflation and employment goals.
